questions.q: A teacher says, ‘Look at the picture. What do you think the people are going to do?’ Which function is this?
‘Work with the person next to you. Compare your answers, then choose one answer together.’ What is the teacher mainly doing?
After explaining a task, the teacher asks, ‘Are you writing alone or with a partner?’ This is an example of:
A teacher asks, ‘If I say I’m exhausted, do I have a lot of energy?’ Which function does this question serve?
The teacher says a sentence and asks the class to repeat it together, then individually. This is:
A learner says, ‘I went to the library yesterday.’ The teacher replies, ‘You went yesterday? Great. What did you borrow?’ The teacher is:
questions.d: Responding naturally and extending learner talk

questions.q: ‘Could you say that again, please? I didn’t catch the last word.’ What is the learner doing?
A learner says, ‘I think the character feels worried because…’ What is the main function of this learner language?
questions.b: Expressing an opinion and supporting it

questions.q: Which teacher instruction is clearest for a lower-level class?
questions.a: Read the text. Then answer questions 1–3.
questions.b: Having completed the reading, proceed to the subsequent comprehension items.
questions.c: Undertake the first stage before responding to the prompts.
questions.d: Engage with the material and fulfil the task requirements.

questions.q: Why should a teacher give task instructions in short, sequenced steps?
questions.a: It makes the task more difficult
questions.b: It prevents learners from asking questions
questions.c: It replaces the need to demonstrate a task
questions.d: Learners can follow the procedure without holding many directions in memory

questions.q: A learner writes ‘becaus’ instead of ‘because’. Which type of mistake is this?
A learner says, ‘She go to work every day.’ Which error is most evident?
A learner says, ‘I don’t know what means this word.’ Which error is most evident?
questions.a: Word order in an indirect question

questions.q: Which teacher response is an effective prompt for self-correction?
questions.d: ‘She go?’ The teacher points to the subject and waits.

questions.q: During a fluency discussion, a teacher writes down recurring errors and discusses them afterwards. This is:
During a controlled accuracy exercise, a learner repeatedly uses the wrong target verb form. Which response is most appropriate?
questions.a: Ignore the error because accuracy is the aim
questions.b: Give brief, immediate correction focused on the target form
questions.c: Wait until next month to mention it
questions.d: Stop the activity and explain every grammar rule

questions.q: A teacher walks around while pairs complete a speaking task, listening and noting progress without interrupting. The teacher is:
Which is the best example of praise that supports learning?
questions.c: ‘Your group is better than the other one.’
questions.d: ‘You used the linking phrase we practised to make your reason clear.’

questions.q: A class agrees to raise a hand before speaking and to listen while a classmate is talking. These are:
A teacher alternates a short listening task, pair discussion and a quick written reflection. This mainly builds:
A learner cannot start a pair task. The teacher gives a small hint, then lets the learner continue independently. The teacher is acting as a:
Which grouping is most suitable when learners need to exchange different information to complete a task?
Why might a teacher put learners in small groups for a problem-solving task?
questions.a: To prevent learners from negotiating meaning
questions.c: To increase learner interaction and share ideas
questions.d: To ensure only the teacher speaks

questions.q: What is the teacher’s main role while learners complete a communicative pair task?
questions.a: Give a new instruction every minute
questions.b: Monitor and provide support when needed

questions.q: A learner says ‘I have 20 years’ to mean their age. The teacher replies, ‘You are 20?’ and continues the conversation. This is:
Which feedback best helps learners improve after a writing task?
questions.c: Give the score without any explanation
questions.d: Point out a repeated verb-tense pattern and ask learners to review examples

questions.q: A teacher asks learners to underline their own examples of past-tense verbs before checking answers. This encourages:
What is the best way to check whether learners understood a new word meaning?
questions.a: Ask learners to copy the word ten times
questions.b: Ask a simple question that distinguishes the meaning from a likely confusion
questions.c: Ask ‘Do you understand?’ and accept silence

questions.q: The teacher asks a learner by name to answer a question. This classroom function is:
Which seating arrangement is most useful for a whole-class discussion where learners should see one another?
questions.c: Pairs facing away from one another

questions.q: ‘What do you notice about the two sentences? Which one sounds more polite?’ The teacher is primarily:
A teacher explains a role-play, models the first exchange, and then asks pairs to begin. The model mainly:
questions.d: Shows learners what to do before they perform the task

questions.q: ‘You have five minutes. Write three ideas, then tell your partner.’ Which instruction sequence is clearest?
questions.b: Write something and continue as usual
questions.c: Time limit, first step, next step
questions.d: Three ideas, partner, five minutes, maybe write

questions.q: The teacher asks, ‘Can the speaker see the word on the board?’ to check the meaning of ‘hidden’. This is:
A learner asks, ‘What does “deadline” mean?’ Which function is the learner using?
‘I’m not sure I agree; the second example seems more formal.’ The learner is:
A learner says, ‘He don’t like coffee.’ What is the main grammatical error?
A learner writes ‘enviroment’. Which error category applies?
Which is a useful way to make instructions accessible without changing the task goal?
questions.a: Use familiar words, one step at a time, and a quick demonstration
questions.c: Give all instructions only in writing
questions.d: Avoid checking whether anyone can begin

questions.q: A teacher says, ‘I went to the market,’ and stresses ‘went’ to draw attention to the irregular past form. This is:
questions.d: Highlighting a language feature through stress

questions.q: A learner says, ‘Could you give me an example?’ What is the learner doing?
Which teacher response best encourages a hesitant learner to continue speaking?
A teacher uses learners’ first language briefly to clarify a safety instruction, then returns to English. This can be appropriate when it:
questions.a: Makes an important instruction clear and supports the lesson aim
questions.b: Replaces all English input in every lesson
questions.d: Is used without considering learner level

questions.q: A learner says, ‘Yesterday I have seen my friend.’ Which feature needs correction?
questions.d: Tense choice in a past-time context

questions.q: The teacher asks, ‘What could you say instead of “very big”?’ This is:
questions.c: Prompting learners to produce a more precise expression

questions.q: A teacher moves closer to a noisy pair, makes eye contact and points to the task sheet without interrupting the class. This is:
Learners know they should open their books, date the page and begin the starter task when the lesson starts. These repeated actions are:
A teacher asks pairs to compare answers before whole-class feedback. This gives learners a chance to:
questions.d: Check and discuss their ideas with a peer

questions.q: A teacher groups learners with different strengths for a collaborative task. The main potential benefit is:
questions.a: The teacher no longer needs to set a task
questions.c: Learners can contribute different knowledge and support one another
questions.d: The stronger learner must do all the work

questions.q: When should a teacher usually monitor a short pair discussion?
questions.a: Only when every learner is silent
questions.b: During the task, observing participation and noting useful feedback

questions.q: A teacher writes ‘sp’ beside a misspelt word and lets the learner correct it. This feedback strategy:
questions.a: Signals the type of error and promotes self-correction

questions.q: Why might immediate correction be avoided during a fluency activity?
questions.b: Grammar is never relevant to speaking
questions.c: The teacher should not listen to learners
questions.d: Frequent interruption can disrupt communication and confidence

questions.q: A teacher gives feedback on whether learners achieved the task outcome, then comments on useful language. The feedback focuses on:
questions.c: Both task success and language use

questions.q: A learner completes a checklist against lesson criteria and identifies one next step. This is:
A teacher gives a quiet learner extra planning time and sentence starters before a discussion. This is an example of:
Which action helps the teacher manage transitions between activities efficiently?
questions.a: Wait until the class becomes noisy
questions.c: Repeat the same instruction several times at random
questions.d: Give a clear signal and explain the next step before learners move

questions.q: A teacher assigns roles such as timekeeper and reporter to group members. This can:
questions.b: Guarantee that no monitoring is needed

questions.q: Which is the best example of constructive peer feedback?
questions.b: ‘Your reason is clear; add an example to support it.’

questions.q: A teacher asks learners to compare today’s speaking recording with an earlier one and note progress. The teacher is encouraging:
For a pronunciation focus, the teacher models a word, marks the stressed syllable and asks learners to repeat it. Which role is most evident?
